svg.title: PMOD-RGBLCD v1.3: where pin 1 of header J2 is

text.font-family: DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: PMOD-RGBLCD v1.3: where pin 1 of header J2 is

text.font-family: DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Pin 1 is the square pad in the corner of the header at the board edge, at the end next to the backlight boost and away from the "PMOD-RGBLCD v1.3" text.

text.font-family: DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The outer column, next to the board edge, is pins 1 to 15. The inner column is pins 30 to 16, so pin 30 is beside pin 1.

text.font-family: DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, Arial, sans-serif
DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Check the orientation before wiring, with a multimeter in continuity mode and nothing powered:

text.font-family: DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 1. Count rows from the end you believe is pin 1. Rows 5 and 14 are GND in both columns: all four pins beep with each other.

text.font-family: DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 2. If instead rows 2 and 11 beep with each other, the board is turned end for end and pin 1 is at the other end.

text.font-family: DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 3. Row 8 tells the columns apart: the outer pin, 8, beeps with GND through the 0 Ω R3; the inner pin, 23, does not. Pin 23 is the 5 V input, through R4.
